transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's project huddle. As we discussed, the school has approved the concept of a twelve-bed teaching garden beside the science wing, and I have final authority to approve the construction, purchasing, and safety plan before we move forward. Before I can sign off on the campus project plan, I need each of you to report any requirements you have verified. Let's start with the science teacher -- what have you confirmed regarding the site and educational needs?

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I need to report a critical site safety finding. Yesterday, after the draft plan was circulated, I received the laboratory results from a soil test I conducted in the proposed garden area. The test measured lead at 180 parts per million. Our district garden standard requires removing the top six inches of soil and using raised beds at that reading. This means the current draft plan's use of in-ground beds does not meet the district standard, and I have not yet entered this result into the project folder.

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I have a critical scheduling and safety update. My utility-locate request just cleared this morning — the site is cleared for work on October 28, but not before that date. Facilities policy requires a posted site permit before any excavation or bed assembly can begin. This means the draft plan's October 18 workday cannot proceed as scheduled; the earliest viable workday is October 28, once the permit is posted.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I have a critical funding update. The community-garden grant award specifies an approved project budget of exactly $4,200 and will reimburse that amount, but only purchases covered by a purchase order issued before ordering can use the grant. The grant office sent me the award confirmation yesterday, and I have not yet attached it to the draft budget. This means the draft plan's $3,000 charge to general funds does not match the grant's approved budget, and we need to update the funding source to the grant's name and the budget to $4,200 before we can proceed.
transcript.speaker: A4

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, I have a critical student-safety update. My student health review, completed this week after the draft equipment list was prepared, identified a documented severe latex allergy among the students scheduled for garden instruction. Under our school safety protocol, this requires nitrile-only gloves instead of the standard latex gardening gloves listed in the draft plan, and an allergy-safety notice posted at the garden entrance.
